related_questions.question: What's the difference between prediabetes and diabetes?

text_blocks.snippet: The primary difference between prediabetes and diabetes lies in the severity of blood sugar levels. Prediabetes is characterized by blood sugar levels that are higher than normal but not yet high enough to be diagnosed as diabetes. In essence, prediabetes is a warning sign that indicates an increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes and other health problems, while diabetes is a condition where blood sugar levels are consistently elevated, requiring management.

list.title: Blood Sugar Levels:
list.snippet: Elevated, but not as high as in diabetes.

list.title: Diagnostic Criteria:
list.snippet: A1C levels between 5.7% and 6.4%, or fasting blood sugar levels between 100 and 125 mg/dL, indicate prediabetes.

list.title: Risk:
list.snippet: Individuals with prediabetes are at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and stroke.

list.title: Reversibility:
list.snippet: Prediabetes can often be reversed with lifestyle changes like diet and exercise.

list.title: Blood Sugar Levels:
list.snippet: Consistently high, exceeding the prediabetes range.

list.title: Diagnostic Criteria:
list.snippet: A1C levels of 6.5% or higher, or fasting blood sugar levels of 126 mg/dL or higher, indicate diabetes.

list.title: Risk:
list.snippet: Diabetes can lead to serious complications like nerve damage, kidney disease, vision loss, and cardiovascular issues.

list.title: Management:
list.snippet: Diabetes requires ongoing management through medication, lifestyle changes, or a combination of both.

text_blocks.snippet: Imagine your blood sugar as a scale. Prediabetes is when the scale is tipped a little bit towards the "high" side, but not enough to be considered dangerously high. Diabetes is when the scale is tipped so far that it's considered a serious problem that needs to be addressed.
